In a new workspace it renders "No working-list size is recorded yet. Add or size the initial account set to evaluate coverage."
findings.problem: totalWorked is not a number of accounts. It is the number of saved ICPs flagged worked (js/demo-seed-runtime.js:191 and js/supabase-config.js:969,978 compute it as icps.filter(worked).length) and src/icp-studio/state.ts:272 adds 1 to it every time 'Save this ICP' is clicked. The quality engine (src/icp-studio/lib/quality.ts:122-132) treats the value as the size of the account list, so the screen makes a statement about the user's account list that is computed from how many ICPs they have saved: both demo books show 'the working account list is small' (value 2) beside 29 watched accounts; each Save click raises the 'list' by one; after 20 saves the criterion turns green. The comment at lines 68-69 repeats the wrong premise ('a running count of accounts worked'). The instruction 'Add or size the initial account set' cannot be followed on this screen because it has no such input. Second defect on the same path: saveDraftAsIcp (src/icp-studio/state.ts:240-252) scores the saved record with draft.engineActive, which this screen never sets, so the stored qualityScore and qualityChecks differ from what the screen showed (executed on the demo ICPs: shown 90 and 92, stored 86 and 88; with a 5,000+ size band and a regional geography the screen shows 'highly specific' (87) and stores 83, 'well defined'). Readiness, Prospecting Desk and Signal Console read the stored score.

findings.state: Default ICP Studio screen, account-match area ('How your N watched accounts match the ICP'); also the ICP chip on the previous and oldest Signal Console account cards
findings.current: hasOverlap(a, b) returns true only when one whole lower-cased string contains the other (lines 138-144). scoreAccountAgainstIcp uses it for industry (line 172) and for headquarters against the ICP geography (line 185). A strong match needs 75 points: industry overlap (60) plus geography overlap (30), or industry overlap plus NO headquarters recorded (15).
findings.problem: Executed on both demo books with the current source (esbuild bundle of icp-match.ts run in node against js/demo-seed-data-ent.js and js/demo-seed-data-smb.js). (1) Industry: an ICP that lists several industries only matches an account whose industry text is a contiguous piece of the ICP text. Enterprise ICP 'Retail / Food Service / Aviation / Logistics': Starbucks ('Food Service / Retail') and Nike ('Apparel / Retail') are classed as not matching. SMB ICP 'Food service / DTC / CPG': Chomps and Siete Foods ('CPG / Food'), Warby Parker ('DTC Eyewear'), Allbirds, Bombas and Rothy's ('DTC …') are classed as not matching — Rothy's and Siete are named in the same seed as wins for this ICP. The screen then lists 'Starbucks — Food Service / Retail' and 'Warby Parker — DTC Eyewear' under 'Accounts that do not match · and why' while the headline says 'We target Retail / Food Service …' / '… DTC …'. (2) Geography: headquarters are stored as 'City, ST' and the ICP geography is 'US', 'North America', etc. 'Chicago, IL' does not contain 'north america' or 'us', so no account with a headquarters can be a strong match for a regional ICP: both books show 0 strong matches for an ICP rated 'highly specific' (11 and 3 accounts stop at 70 points). An account with no headquarters recorded scores higher (75, strong) than one with a US headquarters (70, partial). The only geography hits are accidental letter matches: with ICP geography 'US', 'Austin, TX', 'Houston, TX', 'Columbus, OH', 'Brussels, Belgium' and 'Sydney, Australia' all get the geography points because the letters 'us' appear inside them (executed: a Food Service account in Sydney, Australia scores 90, strong; one in Los Angeles, CA scores 70, partial). The two-letter industry 'AI' matches inside 'Retail'. The user is told '0 strong matches … Refine the ICP or add accounts', but no ICP edit made through the form's menu values and no added account with a headquarters changes this.
findings.governing: AUDIT_BRIEF §5 Function (scoring thresholds, recommendation selection; 'copy that now claims something the code does not do'); ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/original-working-set/04_REWRITE_BATCH_01_SHARED_AND_CORE.md 'Structural rules that cannot be expressed as literal replacement · ICP Studio' (the account-match area must answer how many watched accounts strongly match, partially match, do not match, and why); the module's own header (icp-match.ts:10) documents the intent as 'industry overlap + at least one secondary'
findings.proposed: Two copy edits keep the default screen truthful without changing any score: (a) src/icp-studio/v4/IcpStudioV4.tsx:160 → "No watched account matches this ICP on both industry and headquarters." (drop "Refine the ICP or add accounts", which today cannot produce a strong match for a regional ICP); (b) under the three counts add "Accounts are compared with this ICP by industry and headquarters only." These edits do not correct the wrong classifications. Repair in src/signal-console/lib/icp-match.ts: compare industries term by term — split both strings on '/', ',', '&', '+' and ' and ', and count an overlap when every word of the shorter term appears as a whole word in a term of the other ('Food Service / Retail' then matches an ICP listing 'Retail / Food Service / Aviation / Logistics'; 'CPG / Food' and 'DTC Eyewear' match 'Food service / DTC / CPG'; 'AI' no longer matches inside 'Retail'). Compare geography on whole words, never on letter sequences ('US' must not match 'Austin' or 'Australia'). Score a missing headquarters the same as one that differs (10), not higher. Add src/signal-console/lib/icp-match.test.ts covering these cases (the module has no test file today). OWNER DECISION: (1) approve the term-level industry comparison and whole-word geography comparison above — they implement the 'overlap' the module header documents, but they change which accounts are classed as matching (in the demo Starbucks, Nike, Chomps, Siete Foods, Warby Parker, Allbirds, Bombas and Rothy's leave 'do not match'; Tecovas and Siete Foods lose the accidental 'US' hit); (2) how geography should be recognised — the smallest useful rule is that a headquarters ending in a two-letter US state code (or naming the United States) is inside 'US' and 'North America', Canada and Mexico are inside 'North America', and 'Global' matches every headquarters; EMEA and APAC need a country list. Without such a rule a strong match stays unreachable for every regional geography the older screens offer (North America, EMEA, APAC) and for 'US' except by accident.

findings.problem: The header promises a reason, and the original structural requirement asks the area to answer why. Each row shows only the account's industry, so the reader has to work out the comparison (which ICP field it failed, and whether headquarters was the problem). Nothing says what separates a strong match from a partial one (strong = industry and headquarters both match; partial = industry matches but headquarters does not, or headquarters matches and no industry is recorded). Partial matches — the largest useful group in both demo books — have no reason, and the approved '· monitor' guidance for them was dropped. Nothing on the page says that only industry and headquarters are compared and that company size is ignored, although Company size is one of the ICP fields directly below (high-context dependence; semantic compression).

findings.proposed: Have scoreAccountAgainstIcp also return which comparison passed (add `industry: 'match' | 'differs' | 'not recorded' | 'not compared'` and `geo: …` to IcpMatch — additive, no scoring change) and render the reason on each listed row: not matching → "Notion — industry is Productivity Software"; when the industry matches but the score is still low → "… — headquarters is Malmö, Sweden". findings.problem: The ICP the user sees and edits in ICP Studio is not necessarily the one other areas use. In the enterprise demo the previous Signal Console cards rate accounts against the AI / Software ICP (OpenAI, Databricks, Palantir get the match chip) while ICP Studio lists the same accounts under 'do not match'.
